findings.mechanism: The verb's plural ending carries into its prepositional complement; the preceding Allah-huwa clause and following mā class provide independent register cues, moving from identity to reported invocation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a local move from divine predication to describing the callers' practice.
findings.containment: No cross-ayah discourse shift is claimed.

findings.title: Attributed stability contrast
findings.claim: Beyond truth and falsehood as labels, the focus can carry an attributed contrast between a worship-worthy reality that stands and rival calls toward other/lower objects whose standing does not persist.
findings.mechanism: The supplied before-reading is a bare truth/falsehood opposition; carriers are Allah, al-haqq, al-batil, and dunihi. The independent yadʿūna/min dunihi call contacts worship, reality, nullity, and otherness fields, changing the reading to worship-worthy reality set against substitutes without durable standing.
findings.reader_payoff: The rival direction matters: invoked objects are not neutral alternatives to the named worship-worthy reality.
findings.containment: The ordinary truth/falsehood assertion remains intact. This attributed root pressure does not settle Allah's derivation or claim a physical position for substitutes.

findings.title: Attributed adjudication of claims
findings.claim: A second attributed line reads invocation as rival rights or affiliation claims: al-haqq supplies a due, al-batil an unfounded assertion, and min dūnihi denies parity.
findings.mechanism: Before the trace the sentence reads as invoking false objects besides God; after, callers advance rival claims to worship and the due belongs to God while adverse claims lack title. Yadʿūna's claim branch contacts haqq's owner-bound right, batil's false assertion, and dun's other/lower relation, yielding adjudication.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive invocation as claim-making and the judgment as deciding who has rightful title to worship.
findings.containment: This remains attributed alongside ordinary calling and truth/falsehood. No human disputants are named and genealogical or wartime specializations are not activated.

findings.title: Attributed vertical sovereignty
findings.claim: The closing pair can add sovereign rank and rightful majesty to the visible up/down image: substitutes fall short, while highness and greatness signify prevailing authority.

findings.reader_payoff: The final pair answers the lower relation with dignity, authority, and rightful superiority.
findings.containment: The reading is attributed and coexists with the spatial image; it asserts neither bodily location nor a physical act of subduing.
